title: Implement multi-window burn-rate alerts + paging severity routing for tiered SLOs
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
We need multi-window burn-rate alerting for tiered SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated) and consistent paging severity mapping + on-call routing.

This ticket covers:
- Prometheus recording rules + alert rules for burn rate on primary SLIs (availability/success rate, latency, streaming reliability where applicable)
- Multi-window thresholds per ADR-0143 (fast-burn + slow-burn)
- Routing alerts to correct on-call rotations (SRE primary; add Infra/Fleet + Platform/Routing as secondary responders based on alert type)
- Severity mapping (SEV0/SEV1/SEV2) and what pages vs what goes to Slack-only
- Links to runbooks + consistent annotations (tier, region, endpoint_class)

Non-goals:
- Implementing the budget computation job (ENG-4934)
- Adding tier tags at ingest (ENG-4922)
- Building dashboards (separate ticket/PR in obs-pack)

References:
- Confluence: architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0143-error-budget-burn-rate-alerting-approach
- Confluence: eng-platform/runbooks/error-budget-breach-mitigation-runbook
- Confluence: oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/error-budget-breach-incident-process
acceptance_criteria:
1) Burn-rate alerts exist for each in-scope SLO (Hosted + Dedicated), at least per tier + region + endpoint_class (chat/completions, embeddings, streaming).
2) Alerts use multi-window burn-rate (fast + slow) and are resilient to transient metric gaps.
3) Alert labels include: tier, region, endpoint_class, slo_id (or equivalent), service (gateway/routing/serving) and runbook URL.
4) Paging policy is documented in the alert annotations and in the SRE on-call docs: which alerts page, severity mapping, and how to declare/auto-open incidents.
5) Routing: Dedicated tier burn-rate pages SRE and notifies the Dedicated customer-facing incident channel; Hosted tier pages SRE and posts to eng-sre; capacity-related alerts also notify eng-infra.
6) Alerts are validated in staging and dogfooded in prod in 'notify-only' mode for 1 week before paging hard-enforced (unless policy says otherwise).
implementation_notes:
SLIs / signals (initial):
- Availability / success rate: 1 - (5xx / total), filtered per SLI spec (exclude invalid requests, auth failures, rate-limited, explicit client aborts)
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (gateway ingress -> gateway egress) per endpoint_class; burn-rate approximated via SLO compliance ratio using histogram buckets
- Streaming reliability: stream_disconnect_error_events / stream_start_events (exclude client-cancelled)

Multi-window burn-rate (baseline; adjust after review):
- SEV1 (fast burn): burn_rate > 14.4 for 1h AND burn_rate > 6 for 6h (consumes 2% budget in 1h and 5% in 6h on 30d window)
- SEV2 (slow burn): burn_rate > 3 for 6h AND burn_rate > 1 for 3d
- SEV0 reserved for complete outage / near-total failure rate sustained (separate static availability alert still allowed, but must not replace burn-rate)

Dedicated vs Hosted sensitivity:
- Dedicated: lower tolerance for paging delays; if burn_rate > 14.4 (1h/6h) page immediately.
- Hosted: keep same paging, but add an intermediate 'notify-only' for certain endpoint_class if it’s limited to low-traffic regions during ramp.

Routing / receivers:
- Primary: SRE on-call (PagerDuty: sre-primary)
- Secondary notifications based on alert group:
  - Capacity saturation / queueing symptoms -> notify eng-infra (Slack) + optional PD secondary after triage confirms capacity root cause
  - Routing/fallback flaps or policy eval failures -> notify eng-platform (Slack) and Mina Haddad’s routing on-call alias

Cardinality controls:
- No per-model or per-customer alerting in this phase.
- Break down by tier + region + endpoint_class; optionally by 'service' component for debugging.

PromQL sketch (to be refined to match metric names after ENG-4922 lands):
- Error ratio (5xx):
  sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{status=~"5..",tier=~"hosted|dedicated"}[5m]))
  /
  sum(rate(redwood_api_requests_total{tier=~"hosted|dedicated"}[5m]))
- Burn rate computation uses error_ratio / allowed_error_ratio.

Ops details:
- Alerts must include a stable slo_id label so budget job + dashboards can link.
- Add a 'data_quality' guard: do not page if total request rate < N for the evaluation window; send to Slack instead with low-traffic annotation.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (staging): install recording rules + alerts pointed at test receivers; verify alert labels, grouping, and runbook links.
Phase 1 (prod notify-only): 7 days Slack-only for all new burn-rate alerts (except if SRE leadership approves paging for Dedicated immediately).
Phase 2 (prod paging): enable paging for SEV1/SEV2 Dedicated + Hosted core endpoints in us-east + eu-west; expand regions once noise and grouping are tuned.
Phase 3 (tighten): align thresholds with final SLO targets worksheet; remove legacy static threshold alerts that are redundant or noisy.
risks_and_open_questions:
Q1: How do we handle retries/fallback in SLI accounting? Ensure we measure the user-visible request outcome (per SLI spec) and do not double-count retries.
Q2: Metric gaps: what’s the correct guardrail to prevent paging on missing series (Prometheus scrape gaps, telemetry pipeline delay)? Proposal: require minimum traffic + require series present; otherwise notify-only.
Q3: Latency SLO burn-rate method: histogram-based compliance ratio vs p95 threshold. We should prefer compliance ratio to keep burn-rate math consistent.
Q4: Dedicated routing: do we have an unambiguous tier label at gateway yet? Blocked until ENG-4922 merged and rolled out.
Q5: Incident automation: should SEV1 burn-rate auto-open an incident? Proposal: yes for Dedicated; Hosted: page SRE and let IC declare incident if user impact confirmed.

2026-01-28 (Sergio Costa): Implemented first pass of recording rules in observability-pack branch. Currently keyed by {tier,region,endpoint_class}. Needs metric name alignment after tier tags land in prod.
2026-02-06 (Rafael Mendes): Decision: Dedicated SEV1 burn-rate pages immediately once labels are proven correct; Hosted remains notify-only during first week to tune noise.
2026-02-12 (Aisha Bello): Added traffic floor guardrail to prevent paging in low-traffic regions; still posts Slack notifications with 'low_traffic=true' label for visibility.
2026-02-19 (Aisha Bello): Opened PR with alert rules + annotations + runbook links. Pending review from Sean (paging policy) + Logan (telemetry/metric semantics).
comments: Sean Gallagher (2026-02-07): Make sure severity mapping is explicit in annotations. We’ve had confusion where burn-rate alerts paged as SEV2 but responders treated it as SEV1. Also ensure alerts group by slo_id + tier + region to avoid alert floods.

Logan Wright (2026-02-08): Please avoid per-route labels in the alert itself. We can link to a dashboard panel that shows top contributing routes/models. Alert payload should be stable and low-cardinality.
Mina Haddad (2026-02-09): For routing-related burn (e.g., fallback loops), we need a clear secondary notification to routing on-call. Suggest receiver label routing_team=true for those alert groups.

Neha Kapoor (2026-02-10): Dedicated pages must include customer-impact hint. Even without per-customer, include 'dedicated' tier + region + endpoint_class so CS can correlate quickly. Tie into comms guidelines when impact is sustained >15m.

Jordan Lee (2026-02-18): Deploy gates will consume a 'budget_state' signal from ENG-4934, not the alerts directly. Still, alert naming/labels should match the SLO config schema so we can cross-link in UI and CI logs.
